# PR Sync

Fetch pull requests authored by `bvdh` in the official [HL7/fhir](https://github.com/HL7/fhir) repository and update their local status records.

## When To Use

- Check the current state of pull requests authored by `bvdh` in `HL7/fhir`.
- Refresh local status records after a PR was updated, reviewed, merged, or closed.

## Procedure

1. Run the sync script from the repository root:

   ```bash
   bash ./.github/skills/pr-sync/scripts/sync-prs.sh
   ```

   Before fetching PRs or generating discrepancies, the script requires a successful `jira-sync` within the preceding hour. It checks the modification time of `.github/skills/jira-sync/.last-sync`, which Jira sync writes only after success. The file contents contain only a date, so they cannot establish hour-level freshness.
   If the marker is missing, older than 3600 seconds, or future-dated, run the default incremental Jira sync automatically. Continue only if that succeeds and the marker is fresh; otherwise stop and report the failure, never fall back to stale Jira data.

2. The script uses GitHub CLI authentication to query all PR states, including merged and closed PRs, and writes one status snapshot per PR to `pr/<status>/<number>-<pr-name>/<number>-status.md`, using the PR number as the filename prefix (for example, `4127-status.md`). Status folders are `merged`, `closed`, `open`, and `draft`; draft PRs are open PRs marked as draft and are placed in `draft`.
3. The PR title is lowercased and converted to a hyphen-separated ASCII slug, truncated to 80 characters; titles without ASCII letters or digits use `untitled`.
4. Review the script summary and the refreshed status records. Report the number of PRs synchronized and highlight open, draft, merged, or closed PRs and any failing or pending checks.
5. If `gh` is not authenticated, ask the user to authenticate with `gh auth login` and retry only after authentication succeeds.
6. If the sync stops because the result limit was reached, do not present the partial result as complete; narrow the query or extend pagination before reporting a complete sync.
7. Read `pr/jira-discrepancies.md`, generated by [report-jira.mjs](./scripts/report-jira.mjs). Report the local discrepancies and always present its three clickable Jira search links: add AwaitingMerge, status not Applied, and remove AwaitingMerge. Clearly identify that local counts may be stale and that the links evaluate current Jira values.

## Jira Ticket Consistency

- PR ownership is `bvdh` in `HL7/fhir`. Discover tickets from unique `FHIR-<number>` references in each PR title and description; comments are not treated as ticket scope. Report PRs without ticket references for manual review.
- Open PRs, including drafts: linked tickets must have Status `Applied` and Grouping `AwaitingMerge`.
- Merged or closed PRs: linked tickets must not have Grouping `AwaitingMerge`. Do not impose a Jira status requirement on this scope.
- A ticket referenced by both an open PR and a closed/merged PR follows the open-PR requirements. List overlaps and exclude them from the removal query.
- Compare against canonical local Jira records under `jira/open`, `jira/active`, and `jira/closed`. Report missing, duplicate, or incomplete records as unknown, not compliant.
- Jira records must have been synchronized successfully at most one hour before starting PR sync. This is snapshot freshness, not a claim of a live Jira lookup or complete coverage of every historical PR ticket.
- Persist discrepancy tables with ticket and PR links in `pr/jira-discrepancies.md`. Generate the three Jira search links using all relevant PR-linked ticket keys plus live JQL predicates, not just the locally detected discrepancies. The add-grouping query includes empty Grouping fields.
- This check is read-only against Jira: never change ticket status or grouping automatically. Ask the user to review the results and make the required Jira updates.

## Status Record Behavior

- Each `<number>-status.md` contains the PR URL, title, state, draft status, source and target branches, timestamps, review decision, check states, and sync time, followed by `## Description` and `## Comments` sections with the full PR description and comments.
- The Description section preserves the original Markdown PR body. The Comments section contains discussion comments, submitted reviews, and inline review comments in chronological order. Comments retain their Markdown bodies, author, date, GitHub link, and available review/file/reply metadata.
- Comment endpoints are fully paginated. Empty descriptions and comment lists are explicitly identified in the generated files.
- Description and comments are stored only in the combined status file, not as separate files. Comment entries use level-three headings beneath the Comments section; original Markdown bodies are preserved.
- Legacy PR directories at `pr/<number>-<pr-name>/` are moved to their status folders during sync. Existing PR records are moved when the PR status changes; unrelated content under `pr/` is left untouched. The generated `<number>-status.md` is replaced, and legacy `status.md`, `description.md`, and `comments.md` are removed only after the combined record has been successfully written.
- Description and comment retrieval/rendering must succeed before publishing a PR's files. An API failure stops the sync with an error; PRs already processed may have been refreshed, so do not report a failed run as a complete sync.
- The script refuses to proceed if both the legacy directory and its categorized destination exist, avoiding accidental overwrites.
- GitHub CLI, `jq`, and Node.js are required. The script fails explicitly if a dependency is missing, authentication or the API request fails, or the result limit is reached.
